summary: Closes §4.5 of docs/MYIDSAN_PRODUCTIZATION_PLAN.md ("ZAP scan and k6 load profile"): myidsan was the only one of the four apps with neither an OWASP ZAP plan nor a k6 load profile, despite being the identity provider every other app's login depends on. No Go code changed -- this is dev tooling plus documentation. Adds three ZAP Automation Framework plans (tools/zaproxy/plans/myidsan-{baseline,api,full}.yaml, modelled on the myseliasan equivalents: JSON login at POST /api/login/default, double-submit CSRF via the existing csrf-doublesubmit.js script) and three k6 scripts (tools/k6/scripts/myidsan-{smoke,load,stress}.js), each with a matching config/myidsan.target.env.example, and wires -App myidsan / --app myidsan into tools/zaproxy/scan.ps1|scan.sh and tools/k6/run.ps1|run.sh (default target https://host.docker.internal:3001). tools/k6/scripts/lib/session.js gained a new exported loginFresh(loginPath): unlike the existing ensureLogin (once-per-VU on purpose, so a read test pays bcrypt once), loginFresh performs an unconditional, uncached login and does not fail() on a bad status, because in a stress run at the knee the failures are the measurement -- it exists to isolate the identity provider's LOGIN throughput from its read throughput, which sit an order of magnitude apart (a login storm forces every request through bcrypt; a read-load test only bcrypts once per VU). myidsan-stress.js exposes this as MODE=login (default read). Two IdP-specific hazards, absent from the other three apps' tooling, are carried into the plans/configs/READMEs: (1) exclusions have to cover 'would break the scanner itself' (session revoke, MFA clear, password change, account disable, RBAC-matrix mutation), not just 'destructive' (client-secret rotation, SSO-CA regen), while deliberately leaving /api/auth/authorize, /api/auth/token, the login endpoints, and MFA verification in scope since that is the actual point of scanning an IdP; (2) the failed-login lockout (per IP and per account) must be disabled on the throwaway target before an active scan or a MODE=login run, in addition to the rate limiter, or the run measures the lockout instead of the app. Updated tools/zaproxy/README.md and tools/k6/README.md (both previously documented only mymatasan/myseliasan/myiotsan) with a myidsan section apiece, matching table/file-list entries, and a Files-list correction noting csrf-doublesubmit.js is now shared by myseliasan and myidsan. docs/HOWTO.md and the other supporting specs do not catalogue this per-app tooling today (verified by search) so were left untouched.
compatibility: Documentation and developer-tooling addition only (new YAML/JS/example-env files plus README edits); no application code, config schema, API, or runtime behavior changed for myidsan or any other app. Scope is core,docs rather than myidsan: tools/zaproxy and tools/k6 are explicitly developer-only per their own README preambles ('not part of any shipped app ... not covered by docs/modules/ or the version changelog'), nothing here ships inside a myidsan release artifact, and bumping myidsan's app version would cut a myidsan-v release tag with no actual product change in it -- unlike this stack's earlier docs-only entry (§4.6, reverse-proxy guidance), which shipped deploy/ sample configs an operator deploying myidsan would actually use. A core-only bump updates the shared version but (per .github/workflows/main.yml's tag-idempotence check) tags no product, so no release fires. Existing installs, CI, and every other tool invocation (mymatasan/myseliasan/myiotsan) are unaffected. One pre-existing gap noticed but out of scope to fix here: tools/zaproxy/.gitignore and tools/k6/.gitignore list config/myseliasan.target.env and config/myiotsan.target.env but not the new config/myidsan.target.env -- worth a follow-up so a locally-filled-in myidsan credential file isn't accidentally committable. Two gaps found during the docs pass were closed in the same change rather than left as follow-ups: tools/zaproxy/.gitignore and tools/k6/.gitignore now cover config/myidsan.target.env (a locally filled-in credential file was previously not ignored, verified with git check-ignore), and both runners now forward MODE to the container -- run.ps1 gains a validated -Mode read|login parameter and run.sh forwards the MODE env var -- so the login-storm stress measurement, which is the headline reason for the myidsan scripts, is reachable through the wrappers instead of only via a raw docker compose invocation.
